An online learning platform has observed that a significant number of students enroll in courses but fail to complete them, leading to lower learner engagement and reduced course success rates. The objective of this data science project is to analyze student behavior and develop a predictive model that can identify students who are at risk of dropping out before completing a course.  The platform collects data on student demographics, course categories, login frequency, video watch time, quiz scores, and course completion status. By examining patterns within these variables, the model will predict the likelihood of course completion for each student. This will help the platform take proactive actions such as sending reminders, providing personalized support, or recommending learning resources to improve student retention.  Some challenges and constraints include missing or inaccurate data, differences in learning styles among students, privacy considerations, and the possibility of imbalanced data where non-completers may significantly outnumber completers or vice versa. The solution must be scalable and capable of handling large volumes of student activity data.  The success of the project will be measured using evaluation metrics such as Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-Score, uk and ROC-AUC. From a business perspective, success will also be determined by an increase in course completion rates, improved student engagement, and a reduction in overall dropout rates after implementing targeted interventions based on the model’s predictions.

A mid-sized online learning platform is facing a high course dropout rate, where many students enroll in courses but do not complete them. The goal of this data science project is to build a predictive model that identifies students who are likely to drop out before course completion. The model will use available data such as student demographics, course category, login frequency, video watch time, quiz scores, and past completion records. Key constraints include missing or incomplete data, varying student learning behaviors, and class imbalance between completed and non-completed courses. Success will be measured using classification metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score, along with the platform’s ability to reduce dropout rates through timely interventions and improve overall course completion rates.
